The Financial Times reports that new tax disclosure data shows Apple paid $17 billion in corporate income tax to Ireland last year (2025), accounting for 40% of its total global tax bill. Details below.

Apple: Figures don't reflect full picture

The Financial Times reports that Apple's tax payment to Ireland last year reached $17 billion, with the data coming from reports required by new EU regulations for large companies.

The $17 billion total includes back taxes from a long-running EU dispute. That dispute concluded in 2024, when the EU's highest court ruled that Ireland had provided illegal state aid to Apple and upheld an order requiring the country to recover up to €13 billion in unpaid taxes.

The Financial Times added that, according to the newly filed data, "in the fiscal year ending September 2025, a quarter of Apple's global pre-tax profits were booked through its Irish entities, while only about 3% of its employees were based there."

The Financial Times reports:

During its dispute with the EU, Apple consistently denied receiving illegal state aid and argued that it had complied with Irish tax law. Apple said the relevant profits stemmed from intellectual property developed in the United States and should therefore be taxed in the US.

However, the EU's highest court adopted the European Commission's position. The Commission argued that two Irish tax rulings allowed Apple to attribute the majority of profits recorded by Apple Sales International and Apple Operations Europe to "head office" accounts, even though these "head offices" had no staff and no physical premises.

Returning to today's report, Apple told the Financial Times that the company "has always been one of the largest taxpayers in the world" and argued that the newly disclosed data does not fully reflect its overall tax contributions across countries.

Apple pointed out that these figures only cover corporate income tax calculated by where assets are held, and do not include other taxes (such as value-added tax), which are levied based on where customers are located.
